current.text: He joined Denver this offseason, arriving as Peyton Watson left.
Denver's projected starters are Jamal Murray, Christian Braun, Cam Johnson, Aaron Gordon and Nikola Jokic. DeRozan is projected to come off the bench.

Experts expect him to lead the bench in minutes but in a lower-minute role. They also worry about how his minutes fit with Jokic's. On a more talented team he should produce less than he did in Sacramento.
Even off the bench he should still score and give good FT%.
His upside case: one injury to Braun or Johnson could push him to about 32 minutes, with about 19 points and five assists.
Experts say not to draft him as a top 100 player. Fair value is around rank 135 to 140. Yahoo's rank of 251 was too low and ESPN's top 100 rank and ADP are too high.
In an auction mock, Josh valued him at 1 USD. He went for 3 USD.

Denver's roster is unsettled. Cam Johnson or Christian Braun could be traded, and Moore expects at least two of last year's starters, including Johnson, to be gone by the deadline. A trade like that would open the starter minutes his upside depends on.
Denver has 43 games through March 28 (one below the max) and only 14 back-to-backs, one of the lowest counts in the league.

durable.text: He is a great scorer, but teams must make room for him on offense and defense. He has spacing and defensive limitations.
FT% is his best category: a high percentage on moderate volume. He also keeps turnovers low.
For a forward he is weak in threes and rebounds.

note: DeRozan is a bench scorer in Denver now. Experts put his fair value around rank 135 to 140, which is the edge of our 144-player draft. Pay 1 to 3 USD at most, not the 10 USD he cost in our league last season or the 5 USD Yahoo value. He fits punt 3PM or punt REB builds that want FT%, points and few turnovers. Early in the season, check his bench minutes and watch for injuries to Braun or Johnson or a trade of either one, since those would open the 30-plus minutes his upside needs.
